title: Duress and economic pressure
summary: Duress asks whether an improper threat induced agreement when the affected party lacked a reasonable alternative. Severe commercial pressure requires examination of its source, timing, and available responses.
notes:
In Austin, a supplier threatened to stop deliveries of components needed for the buyer’s naval commitments unless it received price increases and additional business. The buyer’s unsuccessful attempts to obtain timely replacements, its exposure on the main contracts, and the inadequacy of simply suing later were central. A party’s eventual written agreement does not itself settle whether the agreement was obtained through duress.

Distinguish this inquiry from ordinary hard bargaining and from the pre-existing-duty rule. The latter asks what consideration supports a new promise; duress asks about the legitimacy of the pressure that induced assent. The assigned Restatement §§ 175 and 176 are cross-referenced in the syllabus, and their complete text and illustrations are in the Contracts Selections (PDF pages 93–94), linked below.
